originalGroup.material:
The empty seat

Finn takes his lunch to a table in the school garden. There are three children there and one empty seat. "Can I sit here?" he asks.

"Yes," says Ada. She moves her bag from the seat to the ground. Finn sits down. He has rice and chicken. Ada has noodles in a blue box.

A little bird lands near the table. Finn watches it, but he does not give it his lunch. After eating, the children put their rubbish in the bin. Ada picks up her bag. The seat is empty again when they go back to class.

originalGroup.material:
Two clocks in the kitchen

Grandpa has two clocks in his kitchen. One is round and hangs above the door. The other is small and stands beside the bread bin. The round clock says eight o'clock, but the small one says seven.

"Which clock is right?" asks Lily.

Grandpa looks at his watch. It is eight. He puts a new battery in the small clock and moves its hands. Now both clocks show the same time.

Lily helps make breakfast. She puts two cups on the table. "We can have tea now," she says. Grandpa smiles. "Yes. Neither clock can make it for us!"

A ribbon on the bag

At the swimming pool, Hana sees three black bags beside the bench. Her bag is black too. She opens one and finds a large red towel. "This is not mine," she says. Her towel is yellow.

Mum helps her find the right bag. It is behind the bench, not beside the other three. Hana puts on her shoes and takes it home.

At home, she ties a green ribbon to the handle. The next Saturday, she sees the ribbon as soon as she comes out of the pool. She picks up her own bag and waits for Mum by the door.

originalGroup.material:
The biscuit plate

Sam puts six biscuits on a plate. He wants to share them with his two cousins. Before they arrive, he writes their names on three paper cups: Sam, Rose and Ben.

Rose comes first. She brings a bottle of juice. Ben comes with a small football. They all wash their hands, then sit at the table.

"Two biscuits each," says Sam. He puts two beside every cup. There are no biscuits left on the plate.

After their snack, Ben asks to play football. They take the ball to the garden. Rose leaves the juice bottle on the kitchen table, with its lid on.

originalGroup.material:
The puppet’s hat

Nina makes a paper puppet with Dad. It has a round face and a long blue coat. Nina draws black eyes and a small red mouth. Dad cuts out a yellow hat, but Nina does not glue it on.

"He may want a different hat tomorrow," she says. She puts the hat in a little envelope behind the puppet theatre.

In the evening, Nina gives a show for her brother. The puppet goes out in the rain. Nina takes the yellow hat from the envelope and puts it on his head. Her brother claps. "Now he can go to the shop!" he says.

Nina makes a paper puppet with Dad. It has a round face and a long blue coat. Nina draws black eyes and a small red mouth. Dad cuts out a yellow hat, but Nina does not glue it on.

"He may want a different hat tomorrow," she says. She puts the hat in a little envelope behind the puppet theatre.

In the evening, Nina gives a show for her brother. The puppet goes out in the rain. Nina takes the yellow hat from the envelope and puts it on his head. Her brother claps. "Now he can go to the shop!" he says.
questions.explanation: Nina deliberately leaves it separate.
